findings.title: Uprightness in fair measure
findings.claim: At the wider measure-and-weigh passage, the focus's most-upright course can be heard as a practicable standard of fairness in ordinary dealings, not only as a moral superlative.
findings.mechanism: The focus's aqwam meets 17:35's explicit command to complete measure and weigh by a straight balance; that concrete standard makes uprightness operational in exchange.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise of the most upright way acquires a visible social practice: dealings ordered by a straight and fair measure.
findings.containment: This is a contextual application, not a claim that aqwam literally means weighing or that 17:35 exhausts the focus's meaning. The connection supplies target Arabic but not target-side morphology.

epistemic.reason: The cited support is trusted and the focus carrier meets an explicit wider fair-measure image, but the broad systems claim is narrowed and target morphology is not supplied.
